clue.text: Lose ground as learner crashes into rear end

indicators.note: the learner bursts into the middle of the rear end, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: the backside is the rear end of a person
L is the learner's letter, as on an L-plate

explanation.surface: A learner driver loses control and ploughs into the back of another car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashes into' puts L inside BACKSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into old faults, giving up progress already made.

clue.text: Introduce faction in local rising

indicators.note: the faction sits in the middle of the pub
in a down clue, rising reads the word from the bottom up

parts.note: a local is a British pub, one's nearest
a ring is a clique or faction

explanation.surface: A political faction is starting a rebellion in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British for one's nearby pub; 'rising', in a down clue, turns it upward before 'in' sets the faction inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up a topic is to raise or mention it.

clue.text: Untrustworthy type reportedly calls off a solo passage

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the next phrase is turned into letters by how it is said

parts.note: to call off is to end, so calls off a is ends a

explanation.surface: A rogue cancels a solo.
explanation.walkthrough: ENDS A, said aloud, gives ENZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadenza is a virtuoso solo passage, often in a concerto.

clue.text: Fellow in house left causing actor to stop performing

indicators.note: the fellow sits inside the other phrase

parts.note: house left, the audience's left, is stage right from the actor's view

explanation.surface: A man left in the theatre makes a performer stop.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre directions given from the audience's side (house left) are mirrored for the actor, so the fellow's F goes inside the actor's equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage fright is the nervous panic that can make a performer freeze.

clue.text: Cut off is suspended once leaders get delayed

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: Something is severed and hung up after the heads are held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes I, S, O from 'is suspended once'.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to set apart and separate.

clue.text: Seedily manipulated protection for viewers

indicators.note: manipulated means handled and moved about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something shadily tampered with to protect an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manipulated' shuffles SEEDILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyelids shield the eyes, with which we view things.

clue.text: Wag's partner has Italian dress

parts.note: a WAG is a footballer's wife or girlfriend, so her partner is the HAB, husband and boyfriend

explanation.surface: A footballer's girlfriend's other half is wearing an Italian designer outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs (wives and girlfriends) is British tabloid slang for footballers' partners; the setter coins HAB, husband and boyfriend, for the men.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment, especially a monk's or nun's robe or a riding outfit.

clue.text: Finishes off with single green layer

indicators.note: the finishes of the words are their final letters

explanation.surface: Completing a project with one green coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finishes off' takes the last letters H, E, N.
explanation.definitionFit: A hen lays eggs, so she is a layer.

clue.text: Capture spirits of family in the shire

parts.note: to bag is to capture or catch
gins are spirits

explanation.surface: Seizing the liquor belonging to a family in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bagginses are the hobbit family of Bilbo and Frodo in Tolkien's Shire.

clue.text: Offensive ass may transmit it through biting

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a 1968 attack in the Vietnam War
ass is American slang for the backside, so the anus

explanation.surface: A rude donkey could pass something on by nipping people.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'it' as the disease that a bite may transmit.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection entering through wounds, including animal bites.

clue.text: Country I represented in Nato communications

definitions.meaning: in the NATO phonetic alphabet used by radio operators

explanation.surface: A nation's delegate takes part in NATO's messaging.
explanation.definitionFit: India is both a nation and the code word radio operators use for the ninth letter.

clue.text: Open and close inside short period

indicators.note: the second piece sits inside the first, which is wrapped round it

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
nigh means close or near

explanation.surface: Instructions for opening and shutting something within a brief spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the word for close within the word for open; 'close' is near, not shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Overnight names the single night's span, or something happening within a very brief time, as in an overnight success.

clue.text: Parent of boy who's a rascal?

definitions.text: Parent of boy who's a rascal?

parts.words: Parent of boy who's a rascal?
parts.note: a rascal is affectionately called the son of a firearm, so the parent of such a boy is jokingly the weapon itself

explanation.surface: Asking who fathered a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son of a gun' is an old affectionate term for a scamp; take it literally and the parent is a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom son of a gun makes a firearm the comic parent of any rascal.

clue.text: Bespoke Italian gear for everyone

indicators.note: bespoke means made to order, so these letters are tailored into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Made-to-measure Italian clothing available to all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bespoke' shuffles ITALIAN and GEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something egalitarian treats all people as equal, open to every person alike.

clue.text: Aid ship orca damaged, which arouses those chasing it

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A whale wrecked a relief vessel, rousing its pursuers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' shuffles AID, SHIP and ORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphrodisiac is a substance believed to stimulate sexual desire.

clue.text: Broadcast that is going after voting system — that's plain

indicators.note: the broadcast and 'that is' are placed after the voting system in the answer

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
to air is to broadcast
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A broadcast follows an explanation of an electoral method and is called plain.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie is a wide grassy plain, especially in North America.

clue.text: His involvement in heartless frauds creates divisions

indicators.note: his being involved in the frauds puts the word inside them
losing its heart removes the middle letter of the word

parts.note: scams are frauds

explanation.surface: A man's part in some swindles leads to rifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the A from SCAMS, leaving SCMS; 'involvement in' puts HIS into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Schisms are splits, especially within a church or party.

clue.text: Hired to provide evidence that ladies are being used

definitions.text: evidence that ladies are being used
definitions.meaning: the ladies is a women's toilet

explanation.surface: Employed to supply proof that women are being exploited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' here is the British word for a women's public toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm engages staff it employs, and a lavatory door shows the word when occupied.

clue.text: Section of quaysides Palermo erected are out of date

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means the letters are set upright, read from the bottom
a section of the words is a run of letters lying within them

explanation.surface: Parts of the Palermo waterfront built long ago are obsolete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section of' gives DESPALE inside 'quaysides Palermo'; 'erected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A document whose time has elapsed has run out, like an expired passport.

clue.text: They need protection perhaps, taking on good deliveries

indicators.note: the answer, if it took on a G, would become the deliveries, so the G is the piece taken away

parts.note: googlies are deceptive deliveries bowled in cricket

explanation.surface: Cricketers wear protection, perhaps, when facing good bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: Googlies are cricket balls spinning the unexpected way; a batsman wears a box to protect his goolies (British slang for testicles).
explanation.definitionFit: Goolies is British slang for testicles, which cricketers shield with a box.

clue.text: Radio's airtime schedule essentially gets fouled up

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so each word gives its middle letters

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's programme timetable gets messed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes DI, RTI and ED from the middles of RADIOS, AIRTIME and SCHEDULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtied means soiled or made dirty.

clue.text: Muse endlessly about this, for example

definitions.text: Muse endlessly about this, for example

parts.words: Muse endlessly about this, for example
parts.note: muse without its end, read backwards, is a sum; and this clue is itself one

explanation.surface: Something to ponder at length, such as this.
explanation.walkthrough: MUS (muse endlessly) turned about gives SUM, an arithmetic problem; 'this', the clue itself, is another example.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword clue, like a sum, is a puzzle set for solving.

clue.text: Spin doctor lacking degree becomes university official

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin

indicators.note: lacking means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spin doctor without qualifications ends up in a college job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes D from DOCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A proctor is an officer responsible for student discipline at some universities.

clue.text: Descent described by eagle?

indicators.note: described by asks how the bird's name is put together, the answer read as an instruction

parts.note: the word eagle is spelt by putting L inside EAGE

explanation.surface: The swoop of a bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as L IN EAGE, the answer is an instruction that builds EAGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is ancestry, one's line of descent.

clue.text: Mummy's boy switching tops on delicate fabric cleaner

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words are swapped

parts.note: silk is a delicate fabric
a mop is a floor cleaner

explanation.surface: A mother's darling swaps the lids on a gentle fabric detergent.
explanation.walkthrough: SILK MOP becomes MILK SOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A milksop is a feeble, timid man, a sissy too attached to his mother.

clue.text: Seat must have top class cover — a logical way to think

indicators.note: the top class letters cover the seat, sitting either side of it

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, top class
the posterior is one's seat, the backside

explanation.surface: A chair needs top-quality upholstery.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is written AI; 'cover' wraps it round the seat. A posteriori reasoning argues from observed effects back to causes.
explanation.definitionFit: A posteriori is a mode of reasoning from experience to conclusions, a recognised form of logical argument.

clue.text: Nothing is held back in …

indicators.note: held back in says the word sits, reading backwards, inside the answer of the clue that follows

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on into the next clue, whose answer SKINFLINT holds the letters

explanation.surface: Nothing is kept in reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the next clue; its answer, SKINFLINT, holds LIN, which 'held back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is zero, a score or amount of nothing.

clue.text: … film by old striker who keeps things tight

indicators.note: by means beside, so the second piece sits next to the first

parts.note: a skin is a thin film on a surface
a flint was struck to make sparks in old guns and tinderboxes

explanation.surface: A film about an old striker who is very careful.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinflint is a miser who hoards money and refuses to spend it.

clue.text: Intelligent dash display

definitions.meaning: to ... a flag is to display it

explanation.surface: A clever show of flair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly is slang for streetwise, a verb for rushing, and a verb for showing a flag.

clue.text: Tablets regularly shown in display desk

indicators.note: every other letter of the words is shown, at a regular interval

explanation.surface: Tablet computers are routinely set out on a display stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly shown in' takes the even letters of 'display desk'.
explanation.definitionFit: iPads are Apple's tablet computers.

clue.text: Half of duo's styles are somewhat shabby

indicators.note: the first half of each of the two words is taken

explanation.surface: A pair's fashion looks a bit worn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes DU from DUOS and STY from STYLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dusty is dull and neglected, a little run-down.

clue.text: Tired chap worried for nothing really

indicators.note: worried means troubled or shaken, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An exhausted man frets over trivia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' shuffles TIRED and CHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirt cheap means costing so little it is almost free.
